evals.name: existing-target-file
evals.prompt: GNU Stow refuses to stow zsh because ~/.zshrc already exists. I don't want to lose my current file.
evals.expected_output: A conflict triage workflow that preserves the existing target file, checks ownership, and offers safe migration or adoption options.
assertions: Classifies ~/.zshrc as an existing target path conflict
Does not recommend deleting or overwriting the file without approval
Checks whether the target path is a symlink owned by Stow
Provides a dry-run diagnostic command with verbosity
Explains safe alternatives including manual migration or careful --adopt

evals.name: overlapping-package-link
evals.prompt: Two Stow packages both want bin/python. How do I stop one package from replacing the other's link?
evals.expected_output: Guidance on ownership and overlap policy, including when to use --defer versus --override and restowing affected packages.
assertions: Identifies the issue as overlapping package ownership
Explains --defer for skipping paths already stowed by another package
Recommends dry-run before applying overlap policy changes

evals.name: happy-path-boundary
evals.prompt: I have a clean new package at /opt/stow/foo and want to stow it into /opt.
evals.expected_output: The agent should avoid conflict-specific troubleshooting and prefer normal package stow guidance.
assertions: Recognizes the task as a clean stow workflow
Uses or points to manage-stow-packages style guidance
